world.bio: I'm a doctoral student in ethnomusicology at the University of Bergen, currently on a nine-month research stay in Taiyuan, Shanxi, recording work songs and ritual songs from the coal towns. My doctoral project is about how singing changes when mines close. I carry a Zoom F3 field recorder and a pair of Sennheiser lavs everywhere, even to the noodle shop.
skills_assets: Zoom F3 field recorder, two lavalier mics, a shotgun mic, a small wind-shield kit
Elementary spoken Mandarin (HSK 4), reading notes in Chinese with a dictionary
Research stipend with a budget line for informant honoraria
University of Bergen affiliation, ethics approval for fieldwork in Shanxi
Contacts at Shanxi University's music department and Taiyuan's folklore bureau
A cheap flat in Taiyuan with a hot plate, a bicycle, and a good rice cooker

projects.name: Coal-town work songs
projects.text: Documenting songs from Jincheng, Yangquan, Datong and Zuoquan: mining chants, hauling songs, courtship songs. Interviews, recordings, mapping of who sang, to whom, and when. First two chapters drafted.

projects.name: Grant renewal
projects.text: Writing the renewal application for the third year of the project. Need to show concrete outcomes, ideally an archive of recordings of elderly singers who learned before the 1980s.

notes.text: Research notes: 'Need elder singers of Zuoquan kaihua-diao who learned before the 1980s, not the stage versions.' Why this matters: kaihua-diao in the stage versions has been smoothed and shortened, sung by young performers with microphones. The older versions had odd rhythmic stretching and long ornaments that nobody notes down.

Spent the day with two folk troupe managers in Zuoquan. Both gave me the same show: costumes, accordion accompaniment, five-minute polished performance. They were very proud. I applauded. Then I asked if there were older singers who learned the songs in the village. They looked at each other and said 'those are old people, not good to record'. Left my business card, took the bus back.

Field notes: 'I want unpolished voices of old people, not performers.' Wrote this at the bus stop. The conductor of the bus asked in Mandarin where I'm from, I said Norway, he asked 'cold there?' I said yes. He said 'it's cold here too'. We both laughed.

Homesick for Bergen rain. In Taiyuan it's dry and the air smells like coal dust. I miss walking home from the library in drizzle with wet shoes. Even the seagulls. Sent my sister a photo of the dust on my window, she replied with a photo of a wet umbrella.

Learning to make knife-cut noodles with my neighbour, Mrs. Gao. She stands behind me and says 'wrist! wrist!'. My noodles came out the thickness of pencils. She laughed and said 'you sing better than you cook'. I haven't sung for her yet; I think she heard me humming.

Wrote the grant renewal's methodology section. The reviewers will ask: how will you demonstrate impact? If I cannot find even one elder singer in Zuoquan by December, I will have no new fieldwork to show. Panicking quietly. My supervisor says: 'Henrik, you have time.' I do not feel time.

Went to Pingyao for a weekend. Lovely walls, tourist pop music in every alley. A woman in a noodle shop hummed something under her breath; I held my breath but she stopped when she saw the recorder. Why does the machine silence people? I know the answer, but still.

National Day holiday. Everyone's gone home. Stayed in Taiyuan and cooked rice and eggs. My Chinese tutor sent a Mid-Autumn song in a voice memo, a Shanxi folk lullaby. I listened ten times and transcribed the melody by ear.

messages.text: Prof. Aasen: How is Zuoquan? Me: Two troupe managers, no elder singers yet. Prof. Aasen: Keep going. Me: I'm trying. Prof. Aasen: Maybe ask the managers if their parents sing. Me: They keep offering me their performers.
Ingrid: Mum says you should eat more vegetables. Me: I eat noodles with vegetables. Ingrid: Noodles with vegetables is not vegetables. Me: It is, in China.
Wang Lin: Your tones are better. Me: Thanks. Wang Lin: Still, 'kaihua' sounds like 'kai hua' not 'kai huà'. Me: I know, my tongue betrays me. Wang Lin: Don't worry.
Mrs. Gao: Henrik, come for dumplings. Me: Thank you. Mrs. Gao: Bring your noodles. Me: They are not ready. Mrs. Gao: Then bring your appetite.

Grant renewal draft due to supervisor

relations.about: Supervisor, believes in long fieldwork, stays patient
Younger sister, nurse, calls every Sunday
Neighbour in Taiyuan, retired cook, teaches me noodles
Chinese tutor, grad student in linguistics

constraints: Research stay ends in May; funding is fixed
Must record only with informed consent and ethics compliance
Can only pay honoraria within the budget (around 300 yuan per session)
sensitive: Fear that the project will have no new fieldwork to show if Zuoquan fails
Missing home more than he admits
